transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. It's really nice to meet you. Um... well, my mom actually wanted me to come in. I hope that's alright. 

I guess I've just been... well, I don't want you to think I'm just being lazy, because I promise I'm really not, but lately I just can't seem to make myself do anything anymore. It's a little embarrassing to admit, but I mostly just sit in my room all day. Sometimes I even stay in the same clothes... which I know isn't good, I'm sorry. I just haven't been doing the things I usually like, like knitting or journaling, or even going out for walks. 

And when my mom gets worried and asks what's wrong, I just... I barely have the energy to even answer her. I really am trying my best to snap out of it, though. Is... is that the kind of thing you needed to know?
How long have you been feeling this way — sitting in your room, low energy, not enjoying things you used to?

Um, well... I guess it's been a little while now. I really don't want to sound dramatic, but... I think it started around the time I tried to do a community-college program. That was about two years and two months ago. 

I mean, it definitely wasn't this bad at first! I really tried hard to keep up with everything, I promise. But yeah, that's when things sort of... started slipping, I guess. Is... is that too long? I hope it's okay that it took me this long to come in... I just kept hoping I would get better on my own and not have to bother anyone. Does that make sense?

Over these past two years, have there been any stretches of time—say, a few weeks or months—where you felt back to your normal self, or has the low mood and low energy been pretty much constant the whole time?

Um... I really wish I could say yes. I know it would be a lot better if I could tell you I bounced back for a while. But... I think it's pretty much been like this the whole time. 

I mean, I definitely have days where I try really, really hard to push through and act normal so my mom doesn't worry too much! I don't want to be a burden on anyone. But as for actually feeling like my old self on the inside... no, not really. It's just sort of stayed this way. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably makes me sound like I haven't been trying to get better. I promise I have been. Is... is it okay if I say it's just been constant? I hope that's an okay answer.
Within these past two years, has there been any stretch where your mood or energy got noticeably worse than your usual baseline—like a clear dip below how you'd been feeling most of the time?

Um... I don't think so? I mean, I really hope it's alright to say that. I haven't really noticed a time where it got a whole lot worse than... well, than what I just described. It's just been sort of... steady, I guess? 

I really do try my best not to let things get too bad, because I know it stresses my mom out when I seem really down. So I try to keep it from dipping too much, if that makes sense? I'm sorry, I feel like I'm not giving you very helpful answers... but no, I don't think there was a specific stretch where it got noticeably worse than my usual. Is... is that what you were asking? I hope I understood the question right.
During this two-year period, have you also noticed changes in your sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or any thoughts of not wanting to be alive?

Um... well... I guess I haven't really noticed any big changes like that. I mean, my sleep is okay, I think? I try to make sure I go to bed at a reasonable time so I'm not up keeping anyone awake. And I still eat... maybe not a ton, but I make sure to eat when my mom makes dinner so she doesn't feel bad. 

As for concentrating, I guess I'm just mostly in my room, so I don't really have a lot of hard things I need to focus on anyway. And... um, I really don't want you to think I'm completely giving up or anything! I definitely don't have thoughts about not wanting to be here. I promise. I know that would be really awful for my family, and I'd never want to put them through that. 

I just... I try to stay out of the way and keep things as normal as I can. Is it okay that I don't have all those other things going on? I hope I'm not doing this wrong... I really am trying to be helpful.
